subject: no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector

messages.author: b063227c9709ab9e
messages.subject: no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector
parts:
Hi there,

I am running secr density analyses for four different areas within a reserve. Three of the areas have worked perfectly, however, the analyses for the one area keeps giving me the following error: "Error in as.vector(data) :  no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector". 

Example code:

BH_Muz <- read.capthist('Capture_mazunga.csv', 'TrapDepMazunga.csv' , detector = "proximity", fmt = "trapID", trapcovnames =c('habitat', 'site', 'lion', 'leopard', 'spottedhyaena'))

closure.test(BH_Muz, SB=FALSE, min.expected = 2)

maskMuz <- boundary <- readOGR(".", "BHmaskMuz")
BHmaskMuz <- make.mask(traps(BH_Muz),type="polygon", poly=maskMuz, poly.habitat = TRUE)

Following models do give the error:
#spottedhyaena+lion+habitat
secrspottedhyaenalionhabitat <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~spottedhyaena + lion + habitat, mask=maskMuz, verify = FALSE)

#spottedhyaena+lion
secrspottedhyaenalion <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~spottedhyaena + lion, mask=maskMuz, verify = FALSE)

#leopard+lion+habitat
secrleopardlionhabitat <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~leopard + lion + habitat, mask=maskMuz, verify = FALSE)


Following models do not give the error:
#leopard+lion
secrleopardlion <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~leopard + lion, mask=BHmaskMuz, verify = FALSE)

#spottedhyaena+leopard
secrspottedhyaenaleopard <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~spottedhyaena + leopard, mask=maskMuz, verify = FALSE)


Any advice will be greatly appreciated.

All the best,
Jess

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector
parts:
That's a puzzle. I wonder if the code you present is really the code you used. Certainly, it seems unlikely that the secrspottedhyaenaleopard model actually fitted if you really gave the raw (SpatialPolygons?) result from readOGR as the mask. S4 objects are used by package 'sp', 'rgdal' etc. for SpatialPolygons etc., but very little by 'secr' itself. So the problem almost certainly has to do with misuse of the polygon data.
Murray

parts:
Hi Murray,

Thank you for your reply.

It is such a silly mistake and I spent hours trying to figure it out. As you point out it is because I was using the raw SpatialPolygons instead of the make.mask.

All the best,
Jess
